title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
authors: Paul Christiano;Jan Leike;Tom B. Brown;Miljan Martic;Shane Legg;Dario Amodei
abstract: We explore deep reinforcement learning from human preferences by training agents using human preferences between pairs of trajectory segments.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
abstract: We present Constitutional AI a method for training a harmless AI assistant using a constitution of principles.

title: Fairness in Machine Learning: A Survey
abstract: We survey the literature on fairness in machine learning.

title: Equality of Opportunity in Supervised Learning
abstract: We propose a framework for modeling fairness in supervised learning.

title: Why Should I Trust You: Explaining the Predictions of Any Classifier
abstract: We propose LIME a novel explanation technique that explains the predictions of any classifier in an interpretable and faithful manner.

title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
abstract: We present a unified framework for interpreting predictions SHAP.

title: Adversarial Examples are Not Bugs They are Features
authors: Andrew Ilyas;Shibani Santurkar;Logan Engstrom;Brandon Tran;Aleksander Madry
abstract: We argue that adversarial vulnerability is a feature of the data distribution rather than the model.

title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
authors: Deep Ganguli;Liane Lovitt;Jackson Kernion;Amanda Askell;Yuntao Bai;et al.
abstract: We automatically discover cases where a language model is not safe to deploy.
